orders: Measure pupil diameters in bright light and darkness, with assessment of direct and consensual light responses.
Assess near response and perform a light–near dissociation examination.
Perform a complete ocular-motor and neuro-ophthalmic examination, including ocular motility, eyelid position, visual acuity, visual fields, and relative afferent pupillary defect testing.
Perform slit-lamp examination of both irides, including assessment for iris sphincter tears, atrophy, synechiae, inflammation, and pseudoexfoliation.
Instill dilute pilocarpine 0.1% in both eyes and remeasure the pupils after 30–60 minutes.
If the dilute-pilocarpine test is nondiagnostic, perform a 1% pilocarpine test in both eyes.
If pharmacologic testing does not establish the cause, obtain MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast, including the cavernous sinuses and posterior communicating artery regions.

results: 1. Measure pupil diameters in bright light and darkness, with assessment of direct and consensual light responses.

pupil examination (size, light reaction): mild anisocoria; the RIGHT pupil is unreactive to dim light, with involuntary pupillary spasms that are irregular in both frequency and duration and unrelated to eye position
2. Assess near response and perform a light–near dissociation examination.
3. Perform a complete ocular-motor and neuro-ophthalmic examination, including ocular motility, eyelid position, visual acuity, visual fields, and relative afferent pupillary defect testing.
lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides): not recorded
ocular motility examination: exotropia, hypotropia and motility impairment - a right oculomotor nerve palsy

pupil examination (size, light reaction): mild anisocoria; the RIGHT pupil is unreactive to dim light, with involuntary pupillary spasms that are irregular in both frequency and duration and unrelated to eye position
visual acuity and colour vision: normal
4. Perform slit-lamp examination of both irides, including assessment for iris sphincter tears, atrophy, synechiae, inflammation, and pseudoexfoliation.
5. Instill dilute pilocarpine 0.1% in both eyes and remeasure the pupils after 30–60 minutes.
6. If the dilute-pilocarpine test is nondiagnostic, perform a 1% pilocarpine test in both eyes.
7. If pharmacologic testing does not establish the cause, obtain MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast, including the cavernous sinuses and posterior communicating artery regions.
MRI orbits: atrophy of the extraocular muscles, particularly the medial rectus - a long-standing, not acute, palsy
MRI brain with contrast: no lesion, no cranial nerve enhancement
